chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Muyassar, who said:
When Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) arrived at the presence of Abu Ja'far, Abu Ja'far stationed a slave of his above his head and said to him, 'When he comes to me, strike his neck.'

So when Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) entered, he looked at Abu Ja'far and whispered something between himself and his own soul, not knowing what it was. Then he manifested (said aloud), 'O He Who Suffices all His creatures, and no one suffices Him! Suffice me from the evil of Abdullah ibn Ali.'

He said: So Abu Ja'far became such that he could not see his slave, and the slave became such that he could not see him. So Abu Ja'far said, 'O Ja'far ibn Muhammad, I have exhausted you in this heat, so leave.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) exited from his presence.
Abu Ja'far said to his slave, 'What prevented you from doing what I ordered you to do?' He said, 'No, by Allah, I did not see him, and indeed something came and stood between me and him.'
So Abu Ja'far said to him, 'By Allah, if you narrate this hadith to anyone, I will surely kill you.'
ai.seo_question: What happened between Imam al-Sadiq and Caliph al-Mansur during his visit?
ai.summary: This narrative from Al-Kafi describes the visit of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) to the Caliph Abu Ja'far al-Mansur. Upon his arrival, al-Mansur ordered his slave to strike the Imam's neck, but after the Imam whispered a supplication, both the Caliph and the slave became temporarily unable to see each other. The Imam then departed, and when questioned, the slave claimed something had intervened between him and the Imam, leading al-Mansur to warn him to keep the event secret. This event is classically cited by Shia scholars as a demonstration of the Imam's 'ghaybah' (occultation/invisibility) and divine protection, illustrating how the Imam's spiritual authority could temporarily suspend the physical perceptions of the ruling power.
